page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a 500 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing and strong performance in multi-core CPU testing. PassMark CPU and memory scores both rank in the top 25%, alongside strong results in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. For language model workloads, text generation using a small 135M model reaches top-tier speeds, while larger model processing and standard database operations perform within the average range. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput also align with average tier expectations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation combined with a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a dense compute profile without the overhead of memory-heavy configurations. This makes the server suitable for compute-bound workloads that require dedicated processing power rather than massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, ray tracing, multi-threaded text processing, and small-scale language model inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core execution, with notable strengths in software compilation, ray tracing, and small-model text generation. Lacking a GPU, this server relies on its dedicated CPU architecture to deliver consistent, high-throughput compute. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require high memory-to-core ratios. This server is well-suited for software development pipelines, parallel processing tasks, and moderate web serving.
